verdicts.rationale: The paper describes inefficient learning across many variations and suboptimal performance plateaus.
Algorithm 1 specifies these steps, with specialist training conditional on the plateaued generalist remaining suboptimal.
The stated algorithm combinations and online environment sampling are explicitly described.
The main Procgen evaluation selects seven challenging environments; Table 1 specifies 1024 training levels, 1000 unseen levels, and five-run means with standard deviations.
The benchmark description explicitly states V2, the respective skill counts, and evaluation only on training environments.
All four BigFish values match Table 1, whose caption specifies raw episode rewards and five-run means with standard deviations.
The MT-10 and MT-50 percentages and five-run averaging match Table 2; the full context identifies the metric as success rate.
The timing ablation explicitly reports worse sample complexity before plateau and inefficient, ineffective learning from scratch.
All training and test returns match Table 3.
The paper limits ManiSkill testing to PushChair because of simulation and rendering costs, reports 30 steps per second, and uses eight chairs.
The text explicitly requires tuning and describes the stated efficiency costs and potential fine-tuning difficulty.
The authors explicitly say they skip DnC because its quadratic complexity makes their comparison computationally intractable.
The paper defines GSL as the stated meta-algorithm and explicitly identifies specialist-training timing as a key contribution.
